mainTopic: Unclear sales; vows to offer in בית חוניו; and which kinds of idol service disqualify a כהן
overview: The גמרא finishes a discussion about unclear sales. It uses the rule יד בעל השטר על התחתונה, which means the buyer, who holds the document, gets the weaker reading. Then a new משנה teaches that a vowed עולה or נזירות must be completed in the בית המקדש. If the person named בית חוניו in his vow, doing it there counts after the fact. רבי שמעון says such a vow never takes effect. The גמרא asks how offering in בית חוניו can count. רב המנונא says the vow carried no responsibility for the animal, and רבא says the man meant only a gift. רבי יוחנן and a ברייתא rule that he is יצא but gets כרת, and this backs רב המנונא for the עולה. A second משנה rules that כהנים who served in בית חוניו may not serve in ירושלים, but they still eat קדשים like בעלי מומין. The גמרא then discusses which kinds of idol worship disqualify a כהן: רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about unwitting sprinkling and about deliberate slaughter.

steps.title: Why not check which house fell or which slave died?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה בר אבוה: if an unclear sale means the best item, why can the seller hand over a fallen house or a dead slave?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let him see which house fell and which slave died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge against רבה בר אבוה. It uses the earlier ruling that a seller of an unnamed house or slave may hand over the one that fell or died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר אבוה held that an unclear sale refers to the best item. If so, the buyer should get whichever house or slave was best at the time of the sale. He should not be stuck with whichever one happened to fall or die later. So the earlier ruling seems to contradict רבה בר אבוה.

keyTerms.meaning: But why?, a challenge opener
Let him look and see
Which one

phrases.english: But why?
phrases.notes: Why can the seller just hand over the fallen house or dead slave, if רבה בר אבוה says an unclear sale means the best one?

phrases.english: Let him see which house fell,
which slave died!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבה בר אבוה's view on unclear sales.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר אבוה's rule that an unclear sale refers to the best item
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an unclear sale means the best item, the sale should be tied to whichever house or slave was best. It should not default to the one that later fell or died.

steps.title: A buyer is different: the document holder gets the weaker reading
steps.stepSummary: A sale is different, because the buyer holds the document, and a document is read in the way least helpful to its holder.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you talking about a buyer? A buyer is different, because the one holding the document is at a disadvantage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבה בר אבוה's rule does not apply to a buyer. In a sale, the buyer gets the weakest reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule in business law: יד בעל השטר על התחתונה. Whoever holds the document gets the reading least helpful to him. So in a sale, the seller can say he meant the fallen house or the dead slave. This does not cancel רבה בר אבוה's rule. It only shows that his rule is not used in cases of buying and selling.

keyTerms.meaning: A buyer
It is different
The one holding the document has the lower hand; an unclear document is read against him

steps.whatToRemember: יד בעל השטר על התחתונה: when a document is unclear, the person holding it gets the weaker reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of Jewish monetary law for reading unclear contracts.

phrases.english: Are you talking about a buyer?
A buyer is different,
because the hand of the document holder is on the bottom.
phrases.notes: The document holder here is the buyer, since he holds the bill of sale. So he gets the weaker reading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: a sale follows its own rule of narrow reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה בר אבוה's 'best item' rule applies to every unclear transaction, including sales.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a sale, the buyer, as document holder, gets the weakest reading, so the seller may hand over the fallen house or dead slave.

steps.title: Now even עולא's 'attic' can mean the worst room
steps.stepSummary: With the rule יד בעל השטר על התחתונה, the גמרא goes back to עולא's case. The 'attic' there can be read as a plain, poor-quality attic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, you can even say it means an attic, which is the worst one, because the document holder is at a disadvantage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the rule it just stated to fix an earlier problem. It goes back to the challenge from עולא against רבה בר אבוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, עולא's word עלייה was explained as 'the best house' (מעולה), so that it would fit רבה בר אבוה. Now there is no need for that forced reading. עלייה can mean a simple attic, the worst room. That is because עולא's case is also a sale, where the buyer gets the weaker reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this idea
An attic or upper room
Inferior, the worst

steps.whatToRemember: A sale is read narrowly against the buyer. This settles both the fallen house and עולא's attic, and רבה בר אבוה's view still stands for cases other than sales.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
you can even say it means an attic, which is the worst,
phrases.notes: This goes back to עולא's earlier case: 'I sell you a house among my houses; he can show him an עלייה.'

phrases.english: since the document holder is at a disadvantage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the principle from step 2 and uses it to settle an earlier challenge from עולא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the source more simply, using a newly stated principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא's עלייה had to be stretched to mean 'the best house' so it would not contradict רבה בר אבוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: עלייה can mean a plain attic, the worst room, because in a sale the document holder gets the weaker reading.

steps.title: משנה: a plain vow of a עולה must be offered in the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: Someone who says 'הרי עלי עולה' must offer it in the בית המקדש. If he offered it in בית חוניו, he has not fulfilled his vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'I take upon myself a burnt offering', he must offer it in the Temple. If he offered it in the temple of Onias, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its first case is a plain vow to bring a עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain vow means a proper offering in the one place allowed, the בית המקדש in ירושלים. בית חוניו was a temple built in Egypt and is not a valid place. So an offering brought there does not count for this vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
'I take upon myself a burnt offering', a vow to bring a עולה
The temple of Onias, a temple built in Egypt
He has not fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: MISHNA:
'I take upon myself a burnt offering':
he must offer it in the Temple,
and if he offered it in the temple of Onias,
he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the sale discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain vow of a עולה can be fulfilled only in the בית המקדש. Offering it in בית חוניו does not count.

steps.title: A vow worded 'to offer in בית חוניו'
steps.stepSummary: If he vowed a עולה to be offered in בית חוניו, he should still offer it in the בית המקדש. But if he offered it in בית חוניו, he has fulfilled his vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I take upon myself a burnt offering that I will offer in the temple of Onias': he must offer it in the Temple, but if he offered it in the temple of Onias, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. This time the person named בית חוניו in his vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He should still bring the offering in the בית המקדש. But since he only took on a vow to offer it in בית חוניו, offering it there counts as doing what he promised. The only change from step 4 is the wording of the vow, and that changes whether he is יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: That I will offer it
He has fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say it is allowed to offer in בית חוניו. It still says he must bring it in the בית המקדש. 'יצא' only means his vow is now fulfilled after the fact.

phrases.english: 'I take upon myself a burnt offering
that I will offer in the temple of Onias':
he must offer it in the Temple,
but if he offered it in the temple of Onias,
he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלָה שֶׁאַקְרִיבֶנָּה בְּבֵית חוֹנְיוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A contrasting case: the vow names בית חוניו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he vowed to offer in בית חוניו, he should still bring it in the בית המקדש. But offering it in בית חוניו fulfills his vow.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: that vow does not create a עולה at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that a vow to offer a עולה in בית חוניו does not make the animal a עולה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: this is not a burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the second case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said the vow counts and he should bring the offering in the בית המקדש. רבי שמעון says a vow tied to בית חוניו does not create a עולה at all. So according to him, there is no obligation in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not a burnt offering; the vow has no effect

steps.whatToRemember: There are three outcomes in the משנה. A plain vow can be fulfilled only in the בית המקדש. A vow naming בית חוניו, according to the first opinion, can be fulfilled there after the fact. According to רבי שמעון, that second vow creates no עולה at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
this is not a burnt offering.
phrases.notes: He is talking about the second case, the vow that named בית חוניו.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין זוֹ עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion about the case in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow to offer a עולה in בית חוניו does not create any עולה.

steps.title: A plain נזיר must shave in the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: Someone who says 'הריני נזיר' must shave in the בית המקדש. If he shaved in בית חוניו, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person says 'I am a נזיר,' he must do his shaving in the בית המקדש. If he shaved in בית חוניו, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now applies the same pattern it used for a vowed עולה to a נזיר. A regular נזיר who ends his term in בית חוניו has not finished properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the end of his term a נזיר shaves his hair and brings קרבנות. Since he never mentioned בית חוניו, his vow points only to the real בית המקדש, so shaving in בית חוניו does not count. This matches step 4 for the עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who vowed to stay away from wine, haircuts and contact with the dead for a set time
He shall shave; the shaving at the end of the נזירות, done together with his קרבנות
The temple of חוניו in Egypt, which was not a valid place for קרבנות

phrases.english: If one says 'I am hereby a nazirite,' he must shave in the Temple,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם גִּלַּח בְּבֵית חוֹנְיוֹ – לֹא יָצָא.
phrases.english: and if he shaved in the temple of Onias, he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries the עולה ruling of step 4 over to a נזיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain נזיר who shaves in בית חוניו is not יצא.

steps.title: A נזיר who vowed to shave in בית חוניו
steps.stepSummary: If he said 'I am a נזיר on condition that I shave in בית חוניו,' he should shave in the בית המקדש. But if he shaved in בית חוניו, he is יצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person says 'I am a נזיר, and I will shave in בית חוניו,' he should still shave in the בית המקדש. But if he did shave in בית חוניו, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second נזיר case, the one where he named בית חוניו in his vow. It matches step 5 about the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ideal is still the בית המקדש. Because he named בית חוניו himself, shaving there is counted as fulfilling what he said. This 'יצא' is what רבא uses in step 12 to challenge רב המנונא.

keyTerms.meaning: He has fulfilled his obligation
That I will shave; the condition he put into his vow

phrases.english: If one says 'I am hereby a nazirite on condition that I will shave in the temple of Onias,'
he must shave in the Temple,
but if he shaved in the temple of Onias, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting case to step 7, matching step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר who named בית חוניו should shave in the בית המקדש, but he is יצא if he shaved in בית חוניו.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: he is not a נזיר at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says someone who vowed to be a נזיר and shave in בית חוניו is not a נזיר at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: this person is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with step 8, just as he did for the עולה in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון's view, a vow that is tied to an invalid place does not take hold at all. So there is no נזירות here that needs finishing.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not a נזיר; the vow never took effect

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין זֶה נָזִיר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: This one is not a nazirite.

steps.whatToRemember: For both the עולה and the נזיר: with no condition, בית חוניו does not count. If he named בית חוניו, it counts after the fact. רבי שמעון says a vow like that never takes effect.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין זֶה נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreement with the ruling in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of נזירות tied to shaving in בית חוניו does not take effect.

steps.title: How can offering in בית חוניו count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can say 'יצא.' Offering an animal in בית חוניו just kills it; it is not a real קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says he fulfilled his obligation? But he simply killed the animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking the word 'יצא' in the משנה's עולה case (step 5).
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית חוניו is not a valid place for קרבנות, so slaughtering there is just killing an animal. Nothing was really offered, so it seems impossible that the vow was fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
He just killed it; it was slaughtered, not offered

steps.confusionAlert: This question is about the עולה case (step 5), not the נזיר. The נזיר comes up only later, in רבא's challenge.

phrases.english: GEMARA: He has fulfilled his obligation?
But he has merely killed it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by questioning the משנה's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's word 'יצא' about a עולה offered in בית חוניו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaughtering outside a valid מקדש is not a קרבן, so nothing has been fulfilled.

steps.title: רב המנונא: a vow without responsibility
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא explains that by naming בית חוניו, the man is treated as if he said 'I take on a עולה, on condition that I am not responsible for it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: he is treated like someone who said, 'I take upon myself to bring a עולה, on condition that I will not be responsible for it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers the question by changing what 'יצא' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יצא' does not mean he brought a proper קרבן. It means he owes nothing more, because his vow had no responsibility for the animal built into it. Once that animal is gone, he does not have to replace it.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that
Responsibility; the duty to replace the animal if it is lost or ruined
It is upon me; a vow that makes the person himself owe the קרבן

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
He is rendered like one who says:
'It is upon me to bring a burnt offering,
on condition that I will not be responsible for it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲשָׂה כְּאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי עוֹלָה עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא אֶתְחַיֵּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the word 'יצא' in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יצא' means a valid קרבן was brought, which makes no sense in בית חוניו.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יצא' means he has no further duty, because the vow carried no responsibility for the animal.

steps.title: רבא: that cannot work for a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב המנונא: if so, the נזיר case would mean 'I am a נזיר without responsibility for my קרבנות.' But a נזיר cannot finish without his קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If that is so, look at the later part of the משנה, which says that someone who said 'I am a נזיר and will shave in בית חוניו' should shave in the בית המקדש, but if he shaved in בית חוניו he is יצא. Will you also say he is like someone who said 'I am a נזיר on condition that I am not responsible for my קרבנות'? A נזיר who has not brought his קרבנות is not permitted to finish his נזירות!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tests רב המנונא's answer on the נזיר case of the משנה and shows that it breaks down there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a עולה, not being responsible can simply mean no further debt. A נזיר is different: his קרבנות are what release him from נזירות. Without them he stays a נזיר, so 'יצא' cannot just mean 'no responsibility.'

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so; it opens a challenge by following an idea to its result
The later part of the משנה
So too? Would you say the same here?
His קרבנות; the offerings a נזיר brings at the end of his term
Becomes permitted, here meaning free of the נזיר restrictions

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב המנונא's answer fits the עולה case but not the נזיר case, so the גמרא still needs a better explanation of 'יצא.'

phrases.english: Rava said to him: If that is so,
the latter clause, which teaches:
'I am hereby a nazirite on condition that I will shave in the temple of Onias,'
he must shave in the Temple,
but if he shaved in the temple of Onias, he has fulfilled his obligation.
Is he there too rendered like one who says:
'I am hereby a nazirite on condition
that I will not be responsible for its offerings'?
As long as a nazirite does not bring his offerings,
he is not permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב המנונא's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applied to the נזיר clause, it would mean a נזיר is free without his קרבנות. That is impossible, because the קרבנות are needed to release him.

steps.title: רבא: the man only meant to bring a gift
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new explanation of the משנה. The man never made the animal a real קרבן. He only meant to bring a gift, and only if he did not have to travel too far.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This man meant to give a gift. He said to himself: 'If it is enough to bring it in בית חוניו, I will make the effort. More than that, I cannot put myself through.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops רב המנונא's approach and offers his own answer to the question of how the משנה can say 'יצא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא said the animal really is a קרבן, just without responsibility. רבא says the animal was never made holy at all. It was only a promised gift, so bringing it to בית חוניו does not destroy anything holy, and he has kept his word.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift, not a real holy קרבן
It is enough
I will make the effort
To put myself through hardship

steps.confusionAlert: For רבא, 'יצא' does not mean he brought a proper קרבן. It means he kept his word, because he never promised a real קרבן in the first place.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
This person intended it as a gift,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אִי סַגִּיא בְּבֵית חוֹנְיוֹ – טָרַחְנָא,
phrases.english: he said: if it is enough in בית חוניו, I will make the effort,
more than that, I am not able to put myself through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After challenging רב המנונא in Step 12, רבא offers his own answer to the question from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the man's intent: he meant a gift, not a real הקדש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without this, we would think the animal is a real קרבן that gets wasted in בית חוניו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal was never holy, so יצא just means he kept his promise.

steps.title: רבא applies the same idea to the נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the נזיר case the same way. The man never meant to take on real נזירות. He only meant to hold himself back from wine and the like, as long as it was not too much trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נזיר too: this man meant to hold himself back. He said: 'If it is enough in בית חוניו, I will make the effort. More than that, I cannot put myself through.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא carries his 'gift' approach over to the second half of the משנה, the נזיר case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This also answers רבא's own challenge in Step 12. A real נזיר cannot finish without his קרבנות. But this man never became a real נזיר; he only took on some self-denial, so shaving in בית חוניו is enough to keep his word.

keyTerms.meaning: To hold himself back, to deny himself (such as from wine)
Man, person

phrases.english: The nazir also,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי גַּבְרָא לְצַעוֹרֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ קָא מִיכַּוֵּין,
phrases.english: this man intends to hold himself back,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: אִי סַגִּיא בְּבֵית חוֹנְיוֹ – טָרַחְנָא,
phrases.english: he said: if it is enough in בית חוניו, I will make the effort,
more than that, I am not able to put myself through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's explanation from the עולה to the נזיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same redefinition of intent, applied to the second case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נזיר who shaves in בית חוניו should not be able to finish without proper קרבנות.
steps.terutzMaskana: He never took on real נזירות, so shaving in בית חוניו fulfills what he promised.

steps.title: רב המנונא splits the two cases
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא can answer: for the נזיר, רבא is right. But for the עולה, the man is still saying 'a עולה without responsibility for it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב המנונא can tell you: the נזיר is as you said. But for the עולה, he is saying 'on condition that I am not responsible for it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב המנונא against רבא's challenge from Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's challenge only worked against the נזיר case. רב המנונא accepts רבא's reading there, but keeps his own reading for the עולה. So the עולה is a real קרבן, just without responsibility for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Responsibility for replacing it if something goes wrong
As you said

phrases.english: And Rav Hamnuna would say to you:
the nazir is as you said,
the burnt offering: 'on condition that I am not responsible'
for it,' is what he says.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in Step 12 by agreeing to רבא's reading for the נזיר only.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a different explanation for each half of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's challenge in Step 12 seemed to knock out רב המנונא's explanation entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב המנונא's explanation still stands for the עולה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees with רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if someone vowed a עולה for בית חוניו and offered it in ארץ ישראל, he is יצא but also gets כרת. This shows the animal was truly holy, just as רב המנונא says.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן also holds like רב המנונא. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone said 'I take on a עולה that I will offer in בית חוניו,' and he offered it in ארץ ישראל, he is יצא, and he is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב המנונא from a ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only get כרת for offering a truly holy animal outside the בית המקדש. Since רבי יוחנן says כרת, the animal must be a real קרבן, as רב המנונא said. For רבא it was only a gift, so there would be no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off, a heavy punishment from Heaven
Punished
He has fulfilled his obligation

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the man meant only a gift, so the animal is not holy. רב המנונא: for the עולה, it is a real קרבן without responsibility. רבי יוחנן's ruling of כרת backs רב המנונא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the vow really makes the animal holy, so bringing it outside the בית המקדש is a serious sin even though the vow is fulfilled.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan also holds
like this view of Rav Hamnuna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
'I take on a burnt offering that I will offer in בית חוניו,'
and he offered it in Eretz Yisrael,
he has fulfilled his obligation, and is punished with karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב המנונא, the גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן holds the same way.
steps.raayaObject: רב המנונא's view that the עולה is truly holy, just without responsibility
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling (through רבה בר בר חנה) that he is יצא and gets כרת

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the ruling about an offering vowed for the wrong place
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if someone vowed a עולה to bring in the מדבר and brought it in עבר הירדן, he is יצא and also gets כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same thing: if someone said 'I take on a עולה that I will bring in the wilderness' and he brought it in עבר הירדן, he has fulfilled his vow, but he is also punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן's ruling from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the בית חוניו case, the man named a place where you may not bring קרבנות, and he brought it somewhere else outside the מקדש. The ברייתא gives him כרת, and כרת applies only to offering a truly holy animal outside the מקדש. So the animal really was a קרבן, which supports רב המנונא over רבא's 'gift' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering that goes completely on the מזבח
The wilderness, where the משכן once stood
The land on the east side of the Jordan River
He has fulfilled his obligation
Being cut off, a heavenly punishment

steps.whatToRemember: Whether the vow was for בית חוניו or the מדבר, the animal becomes truly holy. So he is יצא, but offering it outside the מקדש brings כרת.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא:
'I take upon myself a burnt offering
that I will offer in the wilderness,'
and he offered it on the other side of the Jordan,
he has fulfilled his vow, and he is punished with כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן's ruling and רב המנונא's view.
steps.raayaObject: That an animal vowed as a עולה for an improper place is truly holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a עולה vowed for the מדבר and offered in עבר הירדן

steps.title: The משנה: כהנים who served in בית חוניו
steps.stepSummary: כהנים who served in בית חוניו may not serve in the מקדש in ירושלים. This is even more true for those who served עבודה זרה. Like בעלי מומין, they get a share of the meat and eat it, but they do not offer.
steps.simpleTranslation: כהנים who served in the temple of חוניו may not serve in the מקדש in ירושלים. It is obvious that the same applies to those who served 'something else', meaning idols. As the פסוק says: 'But the כהנים of the private altars did not go up to the מזבח of ה׳ in ירושלים, but they ate מצות among their brothers.' They are like כהנים with a blemish: they get a share of the meat and eat it, but they do not bring קרבנות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on the status of כהנים who served at the temple of חוניו in מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Serving at בית חוניו takes away a כהן's right to do the עבודה in ירושלים. If serving at a temple built for ה׳ does this, serving idols certainly does. Still, these כהנים remain כהנים: like בעלי מומין, they share in the meat of the קרבנות and eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: A temple built in מצרים by חוניו, a כהן
'Something else', a polite way to say עבודה זרה
כהנים who served at private altars
כהנים with a physical blemish, who may not serve
They get a share of the meat and eat it

steps.confusionAlert: These כהנים are not pushed out of כהונה. They keep their status as כהנים and still eat קדשים. The only thing they lose is the right to do the עבודה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The priests who served in the temple of Onias
may not serve in the Temple in Jerusalem,
and needless to say, those who served 'something else',
phrases.notes: 'Something else' is a polite way of saying idol worship.

phrases.english: as it says: 'But the priests of the private altars did not go up
to the altar of ה׳ in Jerusalem,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִם אָכְלוּ מַצּוֹת בְּקֶרֶב אֲחֵיהֶם״.
phrases.english: but they ate matzos among their brothers.'
These are like priests with blemishes:
they get a share and eat, but they do not offer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about כהנים who served at בית חוניו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים who served at בית חוניו (and certainly those who served idols) may not do the עבודה in ירושלים, but they share in and eat קדשים like בעלי מומין.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a כהן who slaughtered for idols may still serve
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that if a כהן slaughtered for עבודה זרה, a קרבן he later brings in the מקדש is still a ריח ניחוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה says: a כהן who slaughtered for idol worship, his offering is still a pleasing aroma.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from רב יהודה. Slaughtering for an idol does not disqualify a כהן from serving in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that serving idols disqualifies a כהן. רב יהודה limits this: if the only thing the כהן did was slaughter, his later עבודה in the מקדש is accepted. The next step will explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
Slaughtered an animal
A pleasing aroma, meaning the קרבן is accepted

steps.confusionAlert: 'His offering' means a קרבן he brings later in the מקדש for ה׳. It does not mean the animal he slaughtered for the idol.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda says:
A priest who slaughtered for idol worship,
his offering is a pleasing aroma.
phrases.notes: He means a קרבן this כהן later offers in the מקדש is still accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה כֹּהֵן שֶׁשָּׁחַט לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's rule that serving idols disqualifies a כהן: slaughter alone does not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who only slaughtered for עבודה זרה is not disqualified, so his later קרבנות are accepted.

steps.title: The פסוק shows that only real 'service' disqualifies, and slaughter is not service
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבדימי brings the פסוקים in יחזקאל. They disqualify כהנים who 'served' idols, and slaughter does not count as service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר אבדימי says: what is the source? 'Because they served them before their idols and were a stumbling block of sin for the house of ישראל, therefore I raised My hand against them, says ה׳ אלהים, and they shall carry their sin.' And right after it is written: 'And they shall not come near to Me to serve Me as כהנים.' If he did a 'service', yes, he is disqualified. But slaughter is not a service.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר אבדימי gives the source for רב יהודה's ruling. He explains how the פסוק shows that slaughter does not disqualify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק punishes כהנים who 'served' idols by keeping them away from serving in the מקדש. Disqualification comes only from an act that counts as real עבודה. Slaughter is not counted as such a service, so a כהן who only slaughtered for an idol stays allowed to serve.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק that is the source?
Idols
Service, a real act of עבודה
To serve as a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: Only a real act of עבודה done for an idol disqualifies a כהן. Slaughter does not count, so רב יהודה rules that his קרבנות are still accepted.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי: מַאי קְרָאָה?
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi says: What is the verse?
'Because they served them before their idols
and were a stumbling block of sin for the house of Israel,
therefore I have raised My hand against them,
says ה׳ Elokim, and they shall carry their sin.'
And it is written after it:
'And they shall not come near to Me to serve Me as priests.'
If he did a service, yes, he is disqualified;
slaughter is not a service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רב יהודה's ruling and explains how it works.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that slaughtering for idols does not disqualify a כהן
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 44:12-13, which disqualifies only those who 'served'

steps.title: Unwitting sprinkling for idols: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about a כהן who sprinkled blood for עבודה זרה by mistake. Is his later קרבן in the מקדש a ריח ניחוח?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if a כהן sprinkled blood for idols by mistake, רב נחמן says his offering is a pleasing aroma, and רב ששת says his offering is not a pleasing aroma.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת. It is about a כהן who did a real act of service for עבודה זרה, sprinkling blood, but did it unwittingly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 taught that slaughter is not 'service,' so slaughter alone does not disqualify a כהן. Sprinkling blood is real service, so the question here is whether doing it by mistake (שוגג) also disqualifies him. רב נחמן says it does not, and רב ששת says it does.

keyTerms.meaning: He sinned by mistake, without knowing
Sprinkling the blood on the altar, a central act of קרבן service
A pleasing aroma, meaning the קרבן is accepted by ה׳

phrases.english: It was stated: if he acted unwittingly with sprinkling,

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: קׇרְבָּנוֹ רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman says: his offering is a pleasing aroma.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אֵין קׇרְבָּנוֹ רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ.
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet says: his offering is not a pleasing aroma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from slaughter, which is not service, to sprinkling, which is service, done unwittingly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: an unwitting sprinkler's later קרבן is accepted. רב ששת: it is not accepted.

steps.title: רב ששת's proof from the verse in יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת reads 'מכשול עון' as two separate cases. מכשול is a mistake and עון is on purpose, so both kinds of כהן are disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: how do I know this? Because it says, 'and they were to the house of ישראל a stumbling block of sin.' Doesn't it mean either a stumbling block or a sin? 'Stumbling block' means by mistake, and 'sin' means on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a פסוק to prove that even a כהן who served idols by mistake is disqualified from the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק disqualifies כהנים who were 'למכשול עון.' רב ששת splits these into two words, each describing a different sinner. Since מכשול means an unwitting sinner, the unwitting כהן is included in the disqualification.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? This introduces a sage's own source
A stumbling block, read here as an unwitting sin
Sin, iniquity, read here as a deliberate sin
On purpose, deliberately

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: from where do I say it?
As it is written: 'And they were to the house of Israel a stumbling block of iniquity.'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:12. This is the same section that disqualifies כהנים who served idols.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו – אוֹ מִכְשׁוֹל אוֹ עָוֹן,
phrases.english: Is it not saying: either a stumbling block or an iniquity?
And 'stumbling block' means unwitting, and 'iniquity' means deliberate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב ששת's side of the dispute.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's ruling that an unwitting sprinkler is disqualified
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 44:12, 'למכשול עון', read as two separate categories

steps.title: רב נחמן reads the verse as one phrase
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reads 'מכשול עון' as a single idea, a stumbling block of sin. So only the deliberate sinner is meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן? He reads it as 'a stumbling block of iniquity.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב נחמן gets around רב ששת's proof. He reads the two words together, not as two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the phrase means one thing, 'a stumbling block that is a sin,' it only describes a deliberate idolater. The unwitting כהן is then not included in the פסוק's disqualification, so רב ששת's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A stumbling block of sin: the two words read as one description

steps.confusionAlert: Both sages read the same פסוק. They only argue about whether its two words are two separate cases (רב ששת) or one combined description (רב נחמן).

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman: it is a 'stumbling block' of 'iniquity.'
phrases.notes: In other words, one deliberate sin, and not 'either-or.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's reading of the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading of the פסוק, not רב ששת's logic in general.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'either-or' split is not required, because the words can form one phrase about a deliberate sinner.

steps.title: רב נחמן's proof: a כהן atones for himself
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings a ברייתא on the פסוק about unwitting idolatry. It teaches that a כהן can bring his own atonement, which shows he may still serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: how do I know this? As it was taught: 'And the כהן shall atone for the soul that errs, when it sins by mistake.' This teaches that a כהן can gain atonement through himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings his own source. A ברייתא learns from the פסוק about an unwitting sin of idolatry that a כהן may offer his own קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about someone who sinned with idolatry by mistake. The ברייתא learns that a כהן who did this may offer his own atonement-קרבן himself. If he can serve for himself, his unwitting idolatry did not disqualify him, which matches רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall atone
The person who sinned by mistake
Gains atonement
Through himself, by doing the service on his own

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: an unwitting sprinkler for idols may still serve, since the פסוק lets a כהן atone for himself. רב ששת: he is disqualified, since 'מכשול' covers an unwitting sinner.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: from where do I say it? As it was taught:
'And the priest shall atone for the soul that errs
when it sins unwittingly,'

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכֹּהֵן מִתְכַּפֵּר עַל יְדֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: this teaches that a priest gains atonement through himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending against רב ששת's proof, רב נחמן gives a positive source for his own view.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that an unwitting sprinkler's קרבן is a ריח ניחוח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on במדבר 15:28: a כהן who sinned unwittingly in idolatry atones through his own service

steps.title: The ברייתא must be talking about sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן finishes his proof. If the ברייתא were about שחיטה, it would not need to say שוגג, since even מזיד שחיטה does not disqualify. So it must be about זריקה, and a שוגג who sprinkled can still serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did the כהן serve the idol? If you say by slaughtering, why does the ברייתא mention only a mistake? Even on purpose would be fine too! So it must be talking about sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks what kind of idol worship the ברייתא from Step 24 is talking about, and proves it must be זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned in Step 20 that שחיטה does not count as 'service' for this rule. So with שחיטה, even a deliberate כהן could still serve, and the word שוגג would be pointless. That forces the ברייתא to be about זריקה, which shows that a כהן who sprinkled for an idol by mistake may still bring קרבנות. That is רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the animal
Sprinkling the blood, a real act of service
By mistake, without knowing
On purpose, knowingly
Why specifically this case? (the detail seems unnecessary)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב נחמן is saying slaughter for idols is fine. He means only that slaughter does not take away a כהן's right to serve in the מקדש, because it is not counted as 'service'.

phrases.english: In what way did he serve? If you say through slaughter –
why does it mention specifically by mistake?
Even on purpose would also be allowed!
Rather, is it not talking about sprinkling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof רב נחמן started from the ברייתא in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That a כהן who did זריקה for idols by mistake may still serve (רב נחמן)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on the פסוק about unwitting idolatry, read together with the rule that שחיטה is not 'service'

steps.title: רב ששת says the ברייתא is about slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the ברייתא really is about שחיטה. The word שוגג is needed, because a כהן who slaughtered for idols on purpose is disqualified: he became a כומר for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת would tell you: the ברייתא really is about slaughter. And if he did it on purpose, has he not become an idol priest?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת pushes back on רב נחמן's proof by explaining the ברייתא in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's proof depended on the idea that a deliberate slaughterer may still serve. רב ששת rejects that idea. Someone who slaughters for an idol on purpose has become an idol's כומר, so he is disqualified. Now the word שוגג in the ברייתא makes sense even if it is about שחיטה, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping the first idea)
A priest who serves an idol
Idol worship

phrases.english: And רב ששת would say to you:
Actually, it is about slaughter,
and if he did it on purpose, did he not become
a priest of idol worship?!
phrases.notes: He means: of course he did, so a deliberate slaughterer is disqualified, and the word 'by mistake' is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר לָךְ: לְעוֹלָם בִּשְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב נחמן's proof in Step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא must be talking about זריקה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that deliberate שחיטה does not disqualify. רב ששת holds that it does, because the כהן became a כומר.

steps.title: The two אמוראים argue about slaughtering on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב נחמן and רב ששת are each consistent with their own view in a second recorded argument. The case there is a כהן who slaughtered for idols on purpose. רב נחמן says his קרבן is a ריח ניחוח; רב ששת says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow their own reasoning, as it was stated: if a כהן slaughtered for an idol on purpose, רב נחמן says his קרבן is a pleasing aroma, and רב ששת says his קרבן is not a pleasing aroma.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the point they just argued about also appears as a separate, recorded argument between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What divided them in Step 26 was deliberate שחיטה. Here that exact case is quoted as its own argument. רב נחמן allows such a כהן to serve, and רב ששת does not. This confirms that each is being consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning (they are consistent with another view of theirs)
He acted on purpose
A pleasing aroma, meaning the קרבן is accepted

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
as it was stated: if he acted on purpose with slaughter –

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: קׇרְבָּנוֹ רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ,
phrases.english: רב נחמן says: his offering is a pleasing aroma,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אֵין קׇרְבָּנוֹ רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ.
phrases.english: and רב ששת says: his offering is not a pleasing aroma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the argument over the ברייתא to a separate recorded argument between the same אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who slaughtered for idols on purpose: רב נחמן says his קרבן is accepted; רב ששת says it is not.
steps.whatToRemember: The real disagreement is deliberate שחיטה for idols. רב נחמן says it does not disqualify a כהן; רב ששת says it does.

steps.title: The reasons behind each view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts explaining each side. רב נחמן allows the כהן because he did no real 'service' (שחיטה is not service). רב ששת's view is repeated, and his reason continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן says his offering is a pleasing aroma, because he did not do an act of service. רב ששת says his offering is not a pleasing aroma,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats each view in order to give its reason. Here we get רב נחמן's reason, and רב ששת's reason is about to follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's reason ties back to Step 20: only acts of 'service' disqualify, and שחיטה is not one. רב ששת's view is set up again here. His explanation comes right after this, and it will match his point in Step 26 about becoming a כומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Service, an act of avodah
His offering
